page: Microsoft Azure DC64as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DCasv6 series. Powered by AMD processors on the x86_64 architecture, this instance operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The hardware profile supplies 64 dedicated vCPUs alongside 256.0 GB of system memory, sustaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

The instance does not include integrated local disk storage and does not feature GPU accelerators. Storage operations rely on external attachments, with the instance designated as Premium Storage capable. Additionally, the instance configuration provisions zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring virtual network configuration or independently assigned networking resources for public external access.

From an infrastructure perspective, the configuration provides high compute density across 64 dedicated cores without the overhead or power draw of accelerator hardware. A key engineering tradeoff is the total reliance on networked remote storage volumes for I/O operations due to the lack of local ephemeral drives. This architecture fits multi-threaded enterprise application servers, mid-tier database backends, large build systems, and containerized microservice clusters that require balanced memory and CPU allocation.
description: Microsoft Azure DC64as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine within the DCasv6 family, built on the x86_64 AMD processor architecture and managed by Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 64 dedicated vCPUs and 256.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance lacks local ephemeral storage and GPU acceleration, relying on external Premium Storage for block persistence. With dedicated compute capacity and a standard memory-to-core profile, the DC64as_v6 delivers stable compute density for scale-up multi-threaded workloads, though data-intensive applications must account for reliance on networked disk volumes. It is structured for workloads such as large-scale enterprise application serving, relational database engines, microservice container hosts, and CI/CD build environments requiring significant multi-core processing power alongside balanced memory.
